items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Like let me use Ray Brown for example, playing bass. Ray likes to play on top with that fire, because he’s in a little band, you know.

ctx.x: Okay. Why is it that sometimes certain bassists and drummers don’t necessarily swing as well as two other bassists and drummers?

Well because they’re time was different. You see a lot of the time the drummer, you know with a little band a drummer could rush a little bit, really on top. Like let me use Ray Brown for example, playing bass. Ray likes to play on top with that fire, because he’s in a little band, you know. In a big band you can’t play on top, because you’ve got sixteen musicians and the drummer, he’s the most [inaudible] in the band. The guy, he can’t go anywhere but sit on — I call it “sit on it” the tempo, from beginning to…

The bass player almost has got to play the same kind of time as the drummer. You know? In the big band. In a little band they let, I’d say the tempo could go up a little bit because you all do, everybody, and if there’s only four of you you’re all going up. With a big band everybody’s not going up the same way ‘cause you don’t think the same way.
